# Beetle Scan Compare repository instructions

When generating a GitHub Desktop commit message:

- Write a concise imperative Summary no longer than 72 characters.
- Use plain language that identifies the main user-visible outcome.
- Write the Description as 2–5 short bullet points.
- Mention GUI behavior, matching behavior, documentation, icon, packaging, or
  tests only when the selected changes actually affect them.
- State that source images remain read-only when a change affects review or
  file handling.
- Do not claim that a test, DMG build, signature, checksum, commit, push, or
  publication succeeded unless the selected changes or repository evidence
  confirm it.
- Do not mention generated caches, virtual environments, temporary files, or
  internal implementation details unless they are the purpose of the commit.
- Use `FFB` only when referring to forked fungus beetles.
- Keep the tone factual and suitable for a scientific research utility.

Repository conventions:

- Keep the project icon prominently at the top of the README and every
  user-facing how-to HTML page.
- Never commit real beetle scans, personal filesystem paths, exported review
  data, or other research data.
- Ambiguous filename matches must be reported rather than silently guessed.
